syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The definite integral lives behind two doors: Riemann's limit defines it (chop, sample, sum, refine — valid even without anti-derivatives) and the Fundamental Theorem computes it (F(b) − F(a) — valid whenever F exists). The accumulation function is the bridge, the dummy variable distinguishes numbers from functions, and live limits bring the chain rule and the reversal minus.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Adding a constant of integration to a definite integral — it cancels.  ·  Treating the value as a positive area when part of the region lies below the axis.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Adding a constant of integration to a definite integral — it cancels.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The dummy variable*** - integral_a^x f(t) dt is a function of x while integral_a^b f(t) dt is a number - the live limit is the difference.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Forgetting to flip the sign when the limits are given in the order $b$ to $a$.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Riemann sum question? Write Delta x = (b-a)/n and x_i = a + i Delta x first.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Evaluate ∫₁³(2x + 1)dx and interpret the answer geometrically.** — **FTC Part 2:** F(x) = x² + x ⟹ F(3) − F(1) = 12 − 2 = **10**. **Geometry:** the region under y = 2x + 1 from 1 to 3 is a trapezoid with parallel sides f(1) = 3 and f(3) = 7, width 2 ⟹ area = ½(3 + 7)(2) = 10 ✓.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Evaluate lim_{n→∞} Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ (i/n)²·(1/n) by recognising it as a definite integral.** — **Recognise the anatomy:** Δx = 1/n ⟹ b − a = 1 with a = 0; xᵢ = i/n ⟹ right endpoints of [0, 1]; f(xᵢ) = (i/n)² = xᵢ². **Identify:** the sum is the right-endpoint Riemann sum of f(x) = x² on [0, 1].…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For Part 1 with function limits, write the chain-rule factor g'(x) explicitly.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Two doors, one room: Riemann defines, FTC computes - and works even where no anti-derivative exists.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Definite integral = limit of Riemann sums (chop, sample, sum, refine) - the definition; FTC Part 2 = F(b) - F(a) - the computation. FTC Part 1: d/dx of the accumulation function = f(x). Dummy variable: the t in a number-integral is renameable; a variable upper limit makes it a function.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The accumulation function is the bridge object: its derivative is f (Part 1), its value at b is the definite integral (Part 2).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Find d/dx[∫₁^{x²} e^{t}dt] and d/dx[∫ₓ⁵ cos(t²)dt].** — **First (upper limit is a function):** FTC Part 1 + chain rule: f(g(x))·g′(x) = e^{x²}·2x = **2x·e^{x²}**. **Second (lower limit is live):** reversal first: ∫ₓ⁵cos(t²)dt = −∫₅ˣcos(t²)dt ⟹ derivative = **−cos(x²)**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Given ∫₁⁴f(x)dx = 5 and ∫₄⁶f(x)dx = −2, find ∫₆¹f(x)dx and ∫₁⁶f(x)dx, citing the properties.** — **Additivity:** ∫₁⁶f = ∫₁⁴f + ∫₄⁶f = 5 + (−2) = **3**. **Reversal:** ∫₆¹f = −∫₁⁶f = **−3**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to the Definite Integral This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to the definite integral: Riemann sums, the Fundamental Theorem, and the evaluation rules in one page. The parent canonical carries the full treatment; this companion mirrors the theorems, adds the deep readings, and drills four heavy-mark problems.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Definition:** ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx = lim Σf(xᵢ*)Δx — the limit of Riemann sums as the partition refines (n → ∞). - **FTC Part 1:** d/dx[∫ₐˣf(t)dt] = f(x) — differentiation undoes accumulation. - **FTC Part 2:** ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx = F(b) − F(a) for any anti-derivative F — evaluation needs no limit, only the endpoints.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Riemann Sums vs FTC: Two Doors, One Room - The Riemann definition is **local and constructive**: chop, sample, sum, refine — it defines what the integral *is* and works even when no anti-derivative exists (∫e^{−x²}dx has no elementary form yet a perfectly good definite value).…

rows.text: Evaluate lim_{n→∞} Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ (i/n)²·(1/n).  ·  Find d/dx[∫₁^{x²} e^{t}dt].  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — The Dummy Variable and the Boundary Terms - ∫ₐᵇf(t)dt is a **number**; the t is a dummy — rename it freely. But ∫ₐˣf(t)dt is a **function of x** (the upper limit is live). Confusing the two is the classic Part 1 error.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — FTC evaluation:** anti-derivative, endpoints, subtract. - **Type B — Riemann limit:** the right-endpoint sum for x² or x, evaluated as n → ∞. - **Type C — accumulation functions:** d/dx of an integral with variable or function limits.…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"The definite integral needs + C":** no — endpoints subtract the constant away. **"∫ₐˣf(t)dt and ∫f(x)dx are the same kind of thing":** one is a function, the other a family.
